title: Prove and execute the paid clean-row Gray optimum
body:
This PR gives an optimal schedule in the retained paid clean-row connector model. A classical Gray cycle uses `2^n` source calls and `2^n-1` readouts for all nonempty source masks. For uniform complete source price `b>0` and readout price `a>=b`, the exact optimum over all finite legal words is `2^n b+(2^n-1)a`. The proof covers arbitrary linear maps, including singular and noncommuting maps. The original sources, dirty connector and target boundaries are preserved, and the extra row returns to zero. There is no change to the complete kappa calculation.

At five sources the new schedule uses 32 source calls and 31 readouts, versus 160 and 31 in the prior clean schedule. The complete retained root tariff decreases from 38,656 to 34,944, a saving of 3,712. This includes map tables, all row cells, action and mask descriptors, allocation/release and zero writes. The proved dirty-alphabet optimum costs 40,754 in the same fixture, so the new paid-clean schedule saves 5,810 against that stronger comparator. These are declared XOR/storage/scheduler units, not physical machine transitions or a runtime benchmark.

The [proof and full invoice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2a92ad075dc3e881602b8e001c70f127c994e56/research/clean-connector-gray-optimum/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2a92ad075dc3e881602b8e001c70f127c994e56/research/clean-connector-gray-optimum/RESULT.json) and [source manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f2a92ad075dc3e881602b8e001c70f127c994e56/research/clean-connector-gray-optimum/SOURCES.json) state the exact scope. A closed L-step source walk visits at most L-1 nonzero masks; every unvisited output needs at least two readouts. This gives the unbounded-word lower bound when a>=b. An explicit n=3, b=10, a=1 schedule costs 69 versus the Gray cost 87, so the price restriction is material. Heterogeneous tariffs and word-dependent physical compiler costs remain outside the theorem.

Base: canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. Cinna Davis supplied the paid clean-row extension and fixture in [PR #1954](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1954), as recorded in its [source note](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/clean-connector-per-mask-seede54e/README.md). Cinna Davis's [PR #2271](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2271) gives related Gray-tour work under a different borrowed-source/common-ADD contract. Ross Richardson supplied the generic connector in [PR #943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943). Adam Gall supplied the exact dirty-alphabet tariff theorem in [PR #2063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2063); its [proof and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/connector-all-tariff-optimum/README.md) are used for the stronger comparison. The classical reflected Gray cycle and these source results are not claimed as new.

Use standard-library CPython 3.12 from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clean-connector-gray-optimum
```

Expected status: `PASS_CLEAN_CONNECTOR_GRAY_OPTIMUM_NO_NEW_KAPPA`. Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.13 passed: 12 formal words, 18 full-state small optima with no word cutoff, 192 matrix/data cases, all 608 retained basis columns, 64 mixed dirty states and 15 mutation controls. Committed-byte checks, the official 13-file export, Git-free optimized replay, source-hash corruption and typed-receipt corruption controls passed. The original task-card 945-pairing positive control passed separately.

The full predecessor tariff census, physical supplier, selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run. Optional full-history checks are unavailable in this shallow checkout. Recursive hosting, map lowering, descriptor production, precision and a selected caller remain open. The selected frontier is unchanged. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.
